glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.IgG: The main antibody class in blood; can cross the placenta and causes type II reactions.
glossary.Autoantibodies: Antibodies made against the body's own proteins.
glossary.Postsynaptic: On the receiving side of a synapse, here the muscle membrane.
glossary.Acetylcholine: Chemical messenger released by nerves to make skeletal muscle contract.
glossary.Neuromuscular transmission: Passage of a signal from a nerve ending to a muscle fibre.
glossary.Ocular: Relating to the eyes and the muscles that move them.
glossary.Proximal: Closest to the trunk, such as shoulder and hip muscles.
glossary.Beta-blockers: Drugs blocking adrenaline's beta receptors, used for heart conditions; can worsen myasthenia.
glossary.Antimalarials: Drugs used to treat or prevent malaria, such as quinine or chloroquine.
glossary.Lithium: Mood stabiliser used in bipolar disorder; can worsen myasthenic weakness.
glossary.Depolarising neuromuscular blockers: Paralysing drugs used in anaesthesia that work by persistently stimulating acetylcholine receptors.
glossary.Anti-MuSK: Antibodies against muscle-specific kinase, a protein that clusters acetylcholine receptors.
glossary.CT chest: Computed tomography scan of the chest, used to look for a thymoma.
glossary.Forced vital capacity: The most air a person can breathe out forcefully after a full breath in.
glossary.Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor: Drug that stops the enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine, so more remains at the junction.
glossary.Immunosuppressant: A drug that dampens the immune system.
glossary.Intubation: Passing a tube into the windpipe to protect the airway and allow ventilation.
glossary.Ventilation: Mechanical support of breathing with a machine.
glossary.IV immunoglobulin: Pooled donor antibodies given into a vein that dampen the autoimmune attack.
glossary.Hypersensitivity: An excessive or harmful immune reaction.
glossary.Postsynaptic membrane: The muscle membrane under the nerve ending, packed with acetylcholine receptors.
glossary.Synaptic cleft: The tiny gap between the nerve ending and the muscle across which acetylcholine diffuses.
glossary.Fatigability: Weakness that gets worse with repeated use and recovers with rest.
glossary.Receptor clustering: Gathering of acetylcholine receptors into dense patches opposite the nerve ending.
glossary.Thymic hyperplasia: Enlargement of the thymus with extra lymphoid tissue, common in myasthenia.
glossary.Receptor density: How many receptors are packed into an area of membrane.
glossary.Antibody screen: Blood test looking for specific antibodies.
